arxiv-2011-09777.title: Making large overhangs in micrometer and nanometer-sized structures
arxiv-2011-09777.creator: N. Van Horne, M. Mukherjee
arxiv-2011-09777.description: Abstract We describe two general procedures for fabricating microstructures with large overhangs and high aspect-ratio support pillars. The first method uses a static angled dry etch on micro- or nano-pillars to create an initial overhang, followed by wet etching for further erosion.

arxiv-2110-10357.title: Fast Bitmap Fit: A CPU Cache Line friendly memory allocator for single object allocations
arxiv-2110-10357.creator: Dhruv Matani, Gaurav Menghani
arxiv-2110-10357.description: Abstract Applications making excessive use of single-object based data structures (such as linked lists, trees, etc…) can see a drop in efficiency over a period of time due to the randomization of nodes in memory. This slow down is due to the ineffective use of the CPU’s L1/L2 cache.

arxiv-2211-15257.title: Charged-hadron production in p ​ p pp , p p +Pb, Pb+Pb, and Xe+Xe collisions at s NN = 5 \sqrt{s_{{}_{\text{NN}}}}=5 TeV with the ATLAS detector at the LHC
arxiv-2211-15257.creator: The ATLAS Collaboration
arxiv-2211-15257.description: Abstract This paper presents measurements of charged-hadron spectra obtained in p ​ p pp , p p +Pb, and Pb+Pb collisions at s \sqrt{s} or s NN = 5.02 \sqrt{s_{{}_{\text{NN}}}}=5.02 TeV, and in Xe+Xe collisions at s NN = 5.44 \sqrt{s_{{}_{\text{NN}}}}=5.44 TeV.

arxiv-2405-06447.title: Sandboxing Adoption in Open Source Ecosystems Conference: 2024 12th ACM/IEEE International Workshop on Software Engineering for Systems-of-Systems and Software Ecosystems; April 14, 2024; Lisbon, Portugal 2024 12th ACM/IEEE International Workshop on Software Engineering for Systems-of-Systems and So
arxiv-2405-06447.creator: Maysara Alhindi, Joseph Hallett
arxiv-2405-06447.description: Abstract . Sandboxing mechanisms allow developers to limit how much access applications have to resources, following the least-privilege principle. However, it’s not clear how much and in what ways developers are using these mechanisms. This study looks at the use of Seccomp , Landlock , Capsicum , Pledge , and Unveil in all packages of four open-source operating systems.

arxiv-2407-07529.title: Kaluza-Klein Graviton Freeze-In and Big Bang Nucleosynthesis
arxiv-2407-07529.creator: Mathieu Gross 1, Dan Hooper 2,3,4
arxiv-2407-07529.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Mathieu Gross 1, Dan Hooper 2,3,4. In models featuring extra spatial dimensions, particle collisions in the early universe can produce Kaluza-Klein gravitons. Such particles will later decay, potentially impacting the process of Big Bang nucleosynthesis. In this paper, we consider scenarios in which gravity is free to propagate throughout n n flat, compactified extra dimensions, while the fields of the Standard Model are confined to a 3+1 dimensional brane.

arxiv-2507-03397.title: Phase dynamics and their role determining energy flux in hydrodynamic shell models
arxiv-2507-03397.creator: Santiago J. Benavides, Miguel D. Bustamante
arxiv-2507-03397.description: Abstract The transfer of energy and other conserved quantities across scales, also known as flux or spectral flux, is a central aspect of out-of-equilibrium systems such as turbulent hydrodynamic flows. Despite its role in the few predictive theories that exist, a dynamical understanding of what determines said flux (and its direction in scale) has yet to be established.

arxiv-2507-10818.title: How Robust are LLM-Generated Library Imports? An Empirical Study using Stack Overflow
arxiv-2507-10818.creator: Jasmine Latendresse, SayedHassan Khatoonabadi, Emad Shihab
arxiv-2507-10818.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Jasmine Latendresse, SayedHassan Khatoonabadi, Emad Shihab. Software libraries are central to the functionality, security, and maintainability of modern code. As developers increasingly turn to Large Language Models (LLMs) to assist with programming tasks, understanding how these models recommend libraries is essential. In this paper, we conduct an empirical study of six state-of-the-art LLMs, both proprietary and open-source, by prompting them to solve real-world Python problems sourced from Stack Overflow.

arxiv-2507-18216.title: Quantum ergodicity for contact metric structures
arxiv-2507-18216.creator: Lino Benedetto
arxiv-2507-18216.description: Abstract . This paper is dedicated to the proof of a Quantum Ergodicity (QE) theorem for the eigenfunctions of subLaplacians on contact metric manifolds, under the assumption that the Reeb flow is ergodic. To do so, we rely on a semiclassical pseudodifferential calculus developed for general filtered manifolds that we specialize to the setting of contact manifolds.

arxiv-2509-14089.title: The Complexity of Deciding Characteristic Formulae Modulo Nested Simulation (extended abstract)
arxiv-2509-14089.creator: Luca Aceto, Antonis Achilleos, Aggeliki Chalki, Anna Ingólfsdóttir
arxiv-2509-14089.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Luca Aceto, Antonis Achilleos, Aggeliki Chalki, Anna Ingólfsdóttir. This paper studies the complexity of determining whether a formula in the modal logics characterizing the nested-simulation semantics is characteristic for some process, which is equivalent to determining whether the formula is satisfiable and prime.

arxiv-2510-02462.title: Unveiling Dynamics and Variability in Open Clusters: Insights from a Comprehensive Analysis of Six Galactic Clusters 2026 Unveiling Dynamics and Variability in Open Clusters: Insights from a Comprehensive Analysis of Six Galactic Clusters – 18
arxiv-2510-02462.creator: Kuldeep Belwal, D Bisht, Ing-Guey Jiang, R. K. S. Yadav, Ashish Raj, Geeta Rangwal, Arvind K. Dattatrey, Mohit Singh Bisht, Alok Durgapal
arxiv-2510-02462.description: Abstract We present a kinematic and dynamical analysis of six Galactic open clusters—NGC 2204, NGC 2660, NGC 2262, Czernik 32, Pismis 18, and NGC 2437, using Gaia DR3. We used Bayesian and Gaussian Mixture Model (GMM) methods to identify cluster members, but chose GMM because it’s more appropriate for low-mass stars. Estimated distances range from 1.76 to 4.

arxiv-2512-10841.title: Low-Order ℋ 2 / ℋ ∞ {\mathcal{H}}_{2}/{\mathcal{H}}_{\infty}\ Controller Design for Aeroelastic Vibration Suppression
arxiv-2512-10841.creator: Mohammad Mirtaba , Juan Augusto Paredes Salazar , Daning Huang , and Ankit Goel
arxiv-2512-10841.description: Abstract This paper presents an ℋ 2 / ℋ ∞ {\mathcal{H}}_{2}/{\mathcal{H}}_{\infty}\ minimization-based output-feedback controller for active aeroelastic vibration suppression in a cantilevered beam. First, a nonlinear structural model incorporating moderate deflection and aerodynamic loading is derived and discretized using the finite element method (FEM).

arxiv-2602-21207.title: Three-sign cancellation hypernumber systems and associator curvature
arxiv-2602-21207.creator: Jaehwan Kim
arxiv-2602-21207.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Jaehwan Kim. We introduce and study a three–sign cancellation hypernumber system H H which extends the real field by adjoining a third sign Λ \Lambda . The underlying set is H = { 0 } ∪ { + , − , Λ } × ℝ > 0 H=\{0\}\cup\{+,-,\Lambda\}\times\mathbb{R}_{>0} , with a single–valued multiplication and a hyperaddition ⊞ \boxplus designed to encode cancellation phenomena between positive and negative reals.

pmc-10611488.title: Identification of optimal feature genes in patients with thyroid associated ophthalmopathy and their relationship with immune infiltration: a bioinformatics analysis
pmc-10611488.creator: Chao Xiong, Yaohua Wang, Yue Li, Jinhai Yu, Sha Wu, Lili Wu, Boyuan Zhang, Yunxiu Chen, Puying Gan, Hongfei Liao
pmc-10611488.description: BackgroundThyroid associated ophthalmopathy (TAO) is an organ-specific autoimmune disease that has a significant impact on individuals and society. The etiology of TAO is complicated and poorly understood. Thus, the goal of this study was to use bioinformatics to look into the pathogenesis of TAO and to identify the optimum feature genes (OFGs) and immune infiltration patterns of TAO.

pmc-10670816.title: Unsolved Issues in Thymic Epithelial Tumour Stage Classification: The Role of Tumour Dimension
pmc-10670816.creator: Carolina Sassorossi, Pietro Bertoglio, Filippo Lococo, Gloria Santoro, Elisa Meacci, Dania Nachira, Maria Teresa Congedo, Jury Brandolini, Matteo Petroncini, Adriana Nocera, Diepriye Charles-Davies, Piergiorgio Solli, Stefano Margaritora, Marco Chiappetta, Cesar A Moran
pmc-10670816.description: According to the different classifications now in use, thymic tumours are staged by the extent of local invasiveness, and tumour size is not included as a major determinant for the T category. The aim of this double-site retrospective study is to analyse the correlation between tumour dimension and overall survival (OS) in patients who underwent surgical treatment.

pmc-11728468.title: Genome-Wide In Silico Analysis of 1-Aminocyclopropane-1-carboxylate oxidase (ACO) Gene Family in Rice (Oryza sativa L.)
pmc-11728468.creator: Jing Xia, Yingsheng Qiu, Wanli Li, Yingcheng Zhang, Linxin Liu, Yi Wang, Wangshu Mou, Dawei Xue, Yanjie Li
pmc-11728468.description: The plant hormone ethylene elicits crucial regulatory effects on plant growth, development, and stress resistance. As the enzyme that catalyzes the final step of ethylene biosynthesis, 1-Aminocyclopropane-1-carboxylic acid oxidase (ACO) plays a key role in precisely controlling ethylene production. However, the functional characterization of the ACO gene family in rice remains largely unexplored.

pmc-12462316.title: The effects of kinesiology taping on joint stability during descending stairs in patients with acute ankle injuries
pmc-12462316.creator: Ye Wei, Datao Xu, Zhifeng Zhou, Xiuye Qu, Julien S. Baker, Liangliang Xiang, Yaodong Gu
pmc-12462316.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundAcute ankle injuries are common in sports and daily activities. Kinesiology taping enhances lower limb motion patterns, joint stability, and balance during descending stair activity in such patients. The objective of this study was to conduct a comparative analysis of the biomechanical impacts exerted by a KT group and an ST group on the lower limbs of patients with acute ankle injuries while descending stairs.MethodsThe study included 27 participants with acute ankle injuries, who underwent biomechanical assessment under both KT and ST

pmc-12539355.title: Digital Technologies and Student Mental Health: Risks of Social Media and the Promise of Virtual Reality and Autonomous Sensory Meridian Response Interventions
pmc-12539355.creator: Nurbanu Abueva, Anna Buzelo, Yanqiu Wu, Zhanar Turniyazova, Dulat Karakushev, Bojan Obrenovic
pmc-12539355.description: IntroductionThe rapid growth of social media use among students has raised concerns about its impact on mental health. While excessive engagement can increase anxiety and stress, emerging virtual technologies show potential as tools for psychological support.MethodsA mixed-methods experimental study was conducted in a university in Kazakhstan, combining quantitative and qualitative approaches.

pmc-13064315.title: Metabolic effects following initiation of single-inhaler triple therapy in COPD: a prospective observational study
pmc-13064315.creator: Noriane A Sievi, Felix Schmidt, Diego M Baur, Kai Fricke, Jonas Herth, Dora Serényi, Maurice Roeder, Nicole Mosca, Silvan Vesenbeckh, Silvia Ulrich, Christian F Clarenbach, Malcolm Kohler
pmc-13064315.description: BackgroundChronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is characterized by airflow limitation, airway inflammation, and oxidative stress. Triple inhaled therapy improves lung function and reduces acute exacerbations, yet its underlying systemic effects remain poorly understood. Exhaled breath analysis offers a non-invasive approach to assessing treatment-related metabolic changes.

pmc-13198610.title: Dual roles of two Tfdps in germline nuclear meiosis and somatic nuclear fragmentation during sexual reproduction in the unicellular organism Paramecium tetraurelia
pmc-13198610.creator: Xinpeng Zuo, Zihui Wang, Mengyao Liu, Therese Solberg, Danxu Tang, Zhiwei Wen, Chundi Wang
pmc-13198610.description: Meiosis is regulated by phase-specific genes to orchestrate nuclear and cytoskeletal dynamics essential for sexual reproduction. The ciliate Paramecium tetraurelia exhibits nuclear dimorphism, harboring two germline micronuclei (MICs) and one somatic macronucleus (MAC) within a single cell during vegetative growth.

pmc-13563098.title: Altered neuronal start codon stringency favors cap-independent repeat-associated non-AUG translation
pmc-13563098.creator: Clare M Wieland, Shannon E Wright, Sydney Willey, Ishita Purwar, Samantha J Grudzien, Amy Krans, Erinn L Laimon, Melissa J Asher, Adrian M Isaacs, Amanda L Garner, Peter K Todd
pmc-13563098.description: Intronic GGGGCC repeat expansions in C9orf72 cause amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) and frontotemporal dementia (FTD). This expansion supports a non-canonical form of translational initiation known as repeat-associated non-AUG (RAN) translation to produce toxic dipeptide repeat proteins that contribute to neurodegeneration.

pmc-13570047.title: Efficacy and safety of interleukin-6 receptor inhibitors in myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein antibody–associated disease (MOGAD): A systematic review and meta-analysis
pmc-13570047.creator: Aasim Ali, Abdullah Shahid, Javed Iqbal, Asad Ullah Ansari, Maleeha Rauf, Sameen Sarfraz, Anza Amjad, Hafiz Muhammad Yousaf Masood, Muhammad Abdullah Ali, Usama Saleem, Muhammad Asad Shabbir, Muhammad Talha Shabbir, Armaghana Abdullah, Mukesh Kumar Sharma
pmc-13570047.description: BackgroundMyelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein antibody-associated disease (MOGAD) can follow a relapsing course, yet evidence for effective maintenance therapy remains limited. Interleukin-6 receptor (IL-6R) inhibition has emerged as a potential relapse-prevention strategy.ObjectivesTo evaluate the efficacy and safety of tocilizumab and satralizumab in patients with MOGAD.DesignSystematic review and random-effects proportional meta-analysis conducted in accordance with PRISMA 2020.

pmc-13578476.title: A protocol for ploidy determination in ethanol-fixed Atlantic salmon (Salmo salar) fry using propidium iodide and internal standardization: Compatible with field conditions at the sample preservation stage
pmc-13578476.creator: Sebastián Ávila, Maira Toro, Wellison Amorim Pereira, Christian Ellwanger-Reyes, Iván Valdebenito Isler, Elías Figueroa-Villalobos
pmc-13578476.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Highlights•Enables reliable ploidy determination in Atlantic salmon fry using ethanol-fixed blood samples.•Uses internal biological standardization to improve fluorescence normalization and reduce analytical variability.•Enables field preservation of aquaculture samples for later lab analysis.

pmc-13627305.title: Vancomycin-variable enterococci as a silent reservoir of resistance: characterization of the first reported vancomycin-variable Enterococcus faecium isolate in Switzerland
pmc-13627305.creator: Abdessalam Cherkaoui, Patrice François, Gesuele Renzi, Nadia Gaïa, Eve-Julie Bonetti, Diego O. Andrey, Jacques Schrenzel
pmc-13627305.description: ObjectivesThis study reports what is, to our knowledge, the first vancomycin-variable Enterococcus faecium (VVEfm) isolate identified and genomically characterized in Switzerland.MethodsA vancomycin-susceptible, vanA-positive E. faecium isolate recovered from a urine culture was characterized using antimicrobial susceptibility testing (AST), vanA/vanB real-time PCR, population analysis profiling (PAP), spontaneous reversion assays on selective media, and whole-genome sequencing (WGS).
